entries.title: How busy Dubai Marina is (foot traffic & demand)
entries.text: Dubai Marina is one of Dubai's densest mixed-use districts: roughly 70,000 to 100,000+ residents live in the high-rises, and the area draws heavy daytime office traffic plus strong evening and weekend leisure demand. The Marina Walk, JBR (Jumeirah Beach Residence) promenade, and the canal-side restaurants form a continuous high-foot-traffic strip. Seasonality: peak in winter (Nov to Mar) and during major events (Dubai Shopping Festival, Ramadan, Eid); slower in peak summer (Jun to Aug) for outdoor seating, though indoor cafe demand stays steadier. For a specialty cafe this means strong daytime commuter + residential demand and busy weekends, but you should budget for a summer dip on outdoor revenue. These are general-knowledge characterizations, not cited statistics; verify with Dubai Municipality or a local market study if you need hard numbers.

entries.title: Dubai Marina small cafe unit: estimated yearly rent
entries.text: A small cafe unit (roughly 40 to 80 sqm) in Dubai Marina typically rents at about AED 25 to AED 50 per sqm per month for ground-floor F&B space in a mid-tier mall or street-front building, which works out to roughly AED 12,000 to AED 40,000 per month, or about AED 150,000 to AED 480,000 per year. Premium street-front or high-traffic mall locations can exceed this; back-of-house or upper-floor units can be lower. Tenancy is often paid in 4 to 6 cheques (cheque-based rent) and a security deposit of 5 to 10% of annual rent is common. These are estimates from general market knowledge, not a verified listing; confirm against current Dubai property portals (e.g., Bayut, Property Finder) or a Marina F&B broker.

entries.title: Dubai cafe licence: estimated yearly cost
entries.text: Opening a specialty cafe in Dubai typically requires a trade licence issued through a business setup service (mainland DED or free zone). A realistic all-in first-year cost estimate is roughly AED 12,000 to AED 25,000 per year for the base trade licence and standard fees, but a cafe (food & beverage) usually also needs DED trade licence + food safety/health permits (Dubai Municipality), and for F&B the total government + permit fees commonly land around AED 15,000 to AED 40,000 in year one, with renewal fees lower (roughly AED 10,000 to AED 20,000/year) if no scope changes. These are estimates from general knowledge, not a verified quote; the actual figure depends on mainland vs free zone, company size, and exact trade activity. Treat the numbers as unverified until checked against the DED/Dubai Municipality website or a licensed setup consultant.
